title: Tendaguru Beds, Tanzania: Late Jurassic dinosaurs of East Africa
summary: Near Tendaguru hill by Lindi in southern Tanzania, Late Jurassic strata (Kimmeridgian–Tithonian, roughly 157–145 million years old) yielded the dinosaurs Giraffatitan, Dicraeosaurus, Kentrosaurus, Elaphrosaurus and Dysalotosaurus. A Berlin museum expedition dug about 80 square kilometres there in 1909–1913, then German East Africa, and sent about 225 tons of material to Germany.

uncertainty.note: Museum für Naturkunde Berlin states 'roughly 157 to 145 million years old' and Kimmeridgian–Tithonian. No uncertainty is given.

beats.caption: Late Jurassic Tendaguru strata, Kimmeridgian–Tithonian in age, cover about 80 square kilometres around Tendaguru hill near Lindi.
Giraffatitan, Dicraeosaurus, Kentrosaurus, Elaphrosaurus and Dysalotosaurus are the dinosaurs the Berlin museum lists from these beds.
Between 1909 and 1913 a Berlin expedition collected about 225 tons of material, which remains in Germany.
